summary: A humorous seasonal piece on community sports leagues starting September 1, 2023, touring kickball, softball, soccer, pickleball, basketball, volleyball and bowling. It pokes fun at colorful team names, nicknamed captains and amateur enthusiasm, and ends by encouraging readers to sign up and find their team amid the chaos and camaraderie.
one_line: A comic tour of local adult sports leagues and their eccentric teams and captains, encouraging readers to sign up as the season begins.
key_facts: Community sports league seasons begin as of September 1, 2023, according to the piece.
Kickball battles take place at the Maple Street Recreation Center on Saturdays.
The Kicking Kangaroos kickball team is captained by Sally "The Leg" Thompson and is known for a choreographed pregame dance-off.
The Giggle Giants are a kickball team joked to resemble a clown convention.
In softball, Trent "Slugger" Williams plays for the corporate-sponsored team The Bottom Liners.
The Mom Jeans Marauders, led by Carol "The Clobber" Evans, play softball on the East Park diamonds and are praised for their double plays.
The adult soccer league is called The Weekend Peles; its amateur referee is Joe "Whistler" Martinez, and other teams include the Midfield Maestros and the Shin Kickers.
Eva "Paddle Master" Rodriguez leads the pickleball team The Net Ninjas, described as a way to settle disputes with neighbors.
The local basketball league is named The Bouncing Brigade; teams include Three-Point Posse, led by "Downtown" Debbie Hanson, and the Ankle Breakers.
The volleyball team Airborne Aces is captained by Linda "Leapfrog" Leary.
The bowling league The Gutter Gang features Fred "Strike King" Harris, who believes in the magic of his wristband; Spare Me the Drama and Pin Pals compete for a moderately-sized trophy.
The article closes by urging readers to sign up and find their team "or at least a decent pair of cleats."
